slides.0.title: Icewine and Winemaking Craft
slides.0.subtitle: Icewine harvest, pressing and fermentation, plus sparkling and other styles
slides.1.title: Harvesting icewine
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Netting and waiting
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Grapes are netted in autumn against birds and left on the vine until a sustained -8°C or lower, typically December to February; the ideal window is mid-December to early January, and mild weather can push it into February or March. When Inniskillin first tried in 1983 birds ate the grapes, and only with protective netting the next year was Vidal successfully harvested (Wine Country Ontario, Brock University)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Night picking
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The ideal picking temperature is -10 to -13°C (Brock) or -10 to -12°C (Wine Country Ontario), giving juice of about 35–39°Brix. Harvest and pressing take at least six hours and usually happen at night, mostly by hand though machine harvesting is also used (Wine Country Ontario). The Fine Vintage guide adds that grapes must freeze to -8°C for at least 8 hours, a supplementary source
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Cryo-extraction does not count
slides.1.highlights.2.content: "Icewine" and "Eiswein" are protected terms and cannot be used for manually frozen grapes; with deep snow, Quebec growers sometimes pick grapes and freeze them off the vine in hammocks or netting, and such wines do not meet VQA icewine rules. No wine may use the term Icewine on its label unless it is VQA-certified (Fine Vintage, Wine Country Ontario)
slides.1.content: Icewine means naturally frozen on the vine, not a freezer.
slides.2.title: Pressing and fermentation
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Pressing while frozen
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Grapes are pressed in small hydraulic presses; most of the water stays behind as ice and only a little concentrated juice is released, and if the grapes warm during pressing the juice is diluted and quality falls (Wine Country Ontario, Brock). About 10 icewine grapes make 1 ml, against about 1.5 for table wine (Wine Country Ontario)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Juice yield figures
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Yield figures differ: about 15% of a normal yield (Wine Country Ontario, Fine Vintage) or 5–10% (Brock University), so none is tested
slides.2.highlights.2.title: A hard ferment
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The juice is very sweet and hard to ferment; high sugar stresses the yeast, so fermentation often stops early, leaving relatively low alcohol and high residual sugar, and it lasts several months (Wine Country Ontario, Brock). Alcohol is about 9–12% (Fine Vintage says 9–11%, Brock 10–12%). In BC no sugar may be added, residual sugar at bottling must be at least 100 g/L and volatile acidity no more than 2.1 g/L (B.C. Reg. 168/2018, s. 41)
slides.2.content: Icewine trades a whole grape for a few drops of juice.
slides.3.title: Grapes, scale and other styles
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Grapes and scale
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The most common grapes are Vidal Blanc, Riesling and Cabernet Franc, with small lots of Gewürztraminer, Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon; icewine is made in every Canadian wine region and Ontario makes over 90%. Wine Country Ontario gives Ontario an average of about 850,000 L a year, while 2025–26 was 468,752 L (Wine With Seth), so vintages vary a lot; in 2023 Ontario netted 3,320 tonnes of grapes for icewine (Grape Growers of Ontario)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Traditional-method sparkling
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Ontario's traditional-method sparkling relies on Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, Nova Scotia uses L'Acadie Blanc (L'Acadie Vineyards' Prestige Brut Estate is entirely L'Acadie Blanc), and Quebec also makes traditional-method and pét-nat wines. VQA sparkling needs at least 300 kPa from secondary fermentation with natural carbonation (VQA Ontario, Wine With Seth, Luxe Magazine)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Dried grapes and skin contact
slides.3.highlights.2.content: VQA Ontario also has categories such as Vin de Cure or Appassimento (at least 85% dried grapes to use Appassimento) and Skin Fermented White (at least 10 days on skins), showing the region widening its styles; Ontario permits more than 100 varieties (Fine Vintage, 2019) and 74 were actually used in 2025–26 (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.content: Icewine is the signature, but the region's styles are widening.
What must VQA icewine grapes be?
A. Naturally frozen on the vine
B. Frozen in a freezer after picking
C. Dried then frozen
D. Chaptalised
Naturally frozen on the vine; artificial freezing cannot be called Icewine.
Why is icewine often picked at night?
A. Night temperatures are lowest and keep the grapes frozen
B. To avoid birds
C. Sugar peaks at night
D. The law requires it
Picking and pressing at the lowest temperatures avoids dilution.
What happens if icewine grapes warm during pressing?
A. The juice is diluted and quality falls
B. Sugar rises
C. Aroma intensifies
D. Nothing changes
The juice is diluted by melted water.
What is BC icewine's volatile acidity ceiling?
No more than 2.1 g/L (B.C. Reg. 168/2018, s. 41).
What happened when Inniskillin first tried icewine in 1983?
A. Birds ate the grapes
B. Frost destroyed them
C. It was harvested and bottled successfully
D. The government banned it
Only with protective netting the next year did it succeed (Brock University).
When snow is deep, Quebec growers sometimes freeze picked grapes off the vine; what of such wines?
A. They do not meet VQA icewine rules
B. May be called VQA Icewine
C. May be called Appassimento
D. May be called Late Harvest
Because they were not frozen on the vine (Fine Vintage).
